> However, if I use this approach, the y intercept estimates are different.
> I understand that the y-intercepts are constrained. But the y-intercept
> values does not follow either of the vector values above.

No. They are sort of a compromise between the two unconstrained
intercepts. Becasue they must fit well in both groups.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: y-intercept unclear.
parts:
On 10/11/2016 04:30 PM, Sam wrote:
> Thanks for the reply Yves.
>
> If they are a compromise between the two unconstrained intercepts,
> should it not be the average between the two y-intercept matrix?

If they would be the only parameters in the model (ie no factor
loadings, no factor variances/covariances, ...) they would be the
(weighted!) average indeed.

But under equality constraints, we still need to find the best finding
values for each group. The compromise is distributed over many sets of
parameters.

Yves.
